planting.note: Direct sow after all frost danger has passed when soil is warm (65°F+); Dade was bred at a Florida research station for reliable production and better tolerance of the wilt and virus pressure common in hot, humid gardens.

directions: Soak seed overnight to soften the hard seed coat, then direct sow an inch deep in warm, fertile soil in full sun once soil temperatures are reliably above 65°F. Dade was developed at a University of Florida research station and selected for improved tolerance of the fusarium wilt and virus pressure that build up in hot, humid gardens over a long growing season, making it a dependable choice for the Gulf South's extended okra harvest. Plants stay a bit more compact than rangy heirloom types, setting smooth, tapered, medium-green pods that stay tender well past the usual 3-inch mark. Harvest every one to two days once pods start forming to keep plants productive, and remove any pods that slip past picking size, since leaving them on the plant slows new flowering.
